boards.title: Your First Weekend at Oberlin College, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A walkable, under-21-safe sequence of campus landmarks, art, study spaces, and public performances to orient a new Oberlin student.

cards.title: Start with a walk through Tappan Square
cards.subtitle: 13-acre green space linking campus and Oberlin
cards.notes: Begin at the benches and paths to get your bearings, then use the square as the pedestrian link between campus buildings and downtown.
cards.short_summary: A central outdoor starting point for seeing how campus meets town.
cards.evidence_claim: Oberlin identifies Tappan Square as a 13-acre green space connecting the college and the city, with benches, swings, Clark Bandstand, Memorial Arch, and the Rocks.
cards.source_title: Tappan Square | Oberlin College and Conservatory
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public green space; use normal park and campus-safety practices.

cards.title: Find the Memorial Arch
cards.subtitle: Tappan Square landmark
cards.notes: Pause at the arch during your square walk, then continue toward College Street to connect this landmark with the rest of campus.
cards.short_summary: A named landmark within Oberlin's central square.
cards.evidence_claim: Oberlin's Tappan Square facilities page lists the Memorial Arch among the square's features.
cards.source_title: Tappan Square | Oberlin College and Conservatory

cards.title: Orient yourself at Wilder Hall
cards.subtitle: Student Union
cards.notes: Use the Student Union as a navigation checkpoint and look over the nearby campus paths before heading to your next stop.
cards.short_summary: A map-listed student-union landmark near the center of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Oberlin's campus map identifies Wilder Hall as the Student Union.
cards.access_notes: Check building access and any event details before entering.

cards.title: Make a library stop at Terrell
cards.subtitle: 148 W. College St.
cards.notes: Locate the main library early, save its address, and take a short lap through the public-facing areas before you need a study spot.
cards.short_summary: Oberlin's main library is a practical anchor for your first campus loop.
cards.evidence_claim: Oberlin College Libraries lists Mary Church Terrell Main Library at 148 W. College St. and includes it among the college libraries.
cards.access_notes: Consult the library's current hours and access information before visiting.

cards.title: Pick up a snack at Azariah's Café
cards.subtitle: Inside Terrell Main Library
cards.notes: If you want refreshments while exploring Terrell, stop here; check the café's current hours before relying on it for a meal or study break.
cards.short_summary: A named café in the main library offering snacks and beverages.
cards.evidence_claim: Oberlin states that Azariah's Café serves refreshments, snacks, coffee, specialty beverages, and Fresh to Go food items at 148 W. College St.
cards.source_title: Azariah's Café | Oberlin College and Conservatory
cards.access_notes: Located in Terrell Main Library; café hours are posted by Oberlin.

cards.title: Spend time in the Allen Memorial Art Museum
cards.subtitle: Campus art museum
cards.notes: Choose one gallery or exhibition rather than rushing the collection, and check the museum's current visitor information before you go.
cards.short_summary: A free campus museum with collections, exhibitions, and public programs.
cards.evidence_claim: Oberlin says the Allen Memorial Art Museum has been free and open to the public since 1917 and welcomes visitors of all ages.
cards.source_title: Oberlin for the Community | Oberlin College and Conservatory
cards.access_notes: Museum collections, exhibitions, and public programs are described as free and open to the public; confirm current visitor details.

cards.title: See the painted Rocks in Tappan Square
cards.subtitle: Three glacial boulders in Tappan Square
cards.notes: Look at the current messages on the boulders as you cross the square, and treat them as campus landmarks rather than surfaces to climb.
cards.short_summary: Three named boulders that serve as visible message boards in the central park.
cards.evidence_claim: Oberlin documents three Tappan Square boulders—known as the Rocks—that have long carried painted messages about events, congratulations, and birthdays.
cards.source_title: Our Traditions | Oberlin College and Conservatory

cards.title: Check the calendar for a Finney Chapel performance
cards.subtitle: 1,200-seat campus concert and event space
cards.notes: Review the event listing first, then arrive for a concert or recital only when its page confirms admission, tickets, and accessibility details.
cards.short_summary: A major campus venue for student, faculty, and guest-artist performances.
cards.evidence_claim: Oberlin describes Finney Chapel as a 1,200-seat space mainly used for concerts, rehearsals, and events by students, faculty, and guest artists.
cards.source_title: Sacred Spaces | Oberlin College and Conservatory
cards.access_notes: Event access varies; Oberlin's public calendar currently lists some Finney events as free admission with no tickets required.

cards.title: Catch a program at the Cat in the Cream
cards.subtitle: Student-run coffeehouse and performance space
cards.notes: Check the schedule before heading to Hales Annex; choose a free program and arrive with time to settle into the performance space.
cards.short_summary: A student-run campus venue for music, poetry, comedy, theater, and dance.
cards.evidence_claim: Oberlin identifies the Cat in the Cream as its free-admission, student-run performance venue and says it hosts free programs including music, poetry, comedy, theater, and dance.
cards.source_title: Cat in the Cream Coffeehouse | Oberlin College and Conservatory
cards.access_notes: Programs are described as free admission; the coffeehouse also sells beverages and snacks when operating.

cards.title: End with a Warner Concert Hall listing
cards.subtitle: Conservatory performance venue
cards.notes: Use the public events calendar to choose a concert, then verify its listing for date, entry details, and whether tickets are needed before leaving.
cards.short_summary: A named performance venue on Oberlin's public events calendar.
cards.evidence_claim: Oberlin's public calendar lists Warner Concert Hall as the location for Conservatory performances, including a Contemporary Music Ensemble concert marked free admission with no tickets required.
cards.access_notes: Admission varies by event; the cited calendar listing specifies free admission and no tickets required for the Contemporary Music Ensemble concert.
